summary: Jeffrey Hopkins (1940–2024) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1972) and studied under Geshe Wangyal, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Kelden. He served at the University of Virginia from 1973 to 2005.

Jeffrey J. Kripal (born 1962) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1987–1993). In ~2002, he held a chair and department headship at Rice University.

Jeffrey Kotyk works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA from Komazawa University (2015–2016) and a PhD from Leiden University (-2017) under James A. Benn. His posts include McMaster University (attested 2019) and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman (born 1944) held posts at Cornell University (~1968–1973), Yale University (~1974–1977), and Johns Hopkins University (~1977–1983). In ~1984, he became University Professor and Professor of French Literature at Boston University, alongside several visiting professorships.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson (born 1941) is an Indologist who studied at Harvard (BA ~1960–1964; PhD ~1964–1970) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, as well as in France, India, and Toronto. He held posts at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and UC Berkeley (1981–1992).

Jeffrey Newmark is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (~1992–1996) and the University of British Columbia (~2003–2009), later holding a post at the University of Winnipeg (~2011).

Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held a post as a visiting assistant professor of religion at the University of Virginia (attested 2003) and holds a post at Berry College.

Jeffrey Samuels specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Karen C. Lang (attested 2002), also studying under W. S. Karunatillake, and served at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Stout (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Brown University (~1968–1972) and earned his PhD at Princeton University (~1972–1976), where he subsequently served as a professor from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and UCLA (PhD attested 2013) under Gregory Schopen. He held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego (attested 2013).

Jenkuan Shih is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Shih earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, having also studied under MA supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Jennifer Jung-Kim works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, including assistant director (attested 2016) and Lecturer (attested 2026).

Jens Braarvig (born 1948) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts as professor at the University of Oslo (2003) and at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (attested 2004).

Jens Peter Laut (born 1954) is a scholar in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2008) and the University of Göttingen (~2008–2020).

Jens Schlieter (born 1966) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1993–1999) under Josef Simon. He held posts at Bonn, Munich, Bayreuth, and became a professor at the University of Bern (~2007).

Jens-Uwe Hartmann (born 1953) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Munich and completed his habilitation at Göttingen (~1985–1992). He held professorships at Humboldt University (1995–2001), Free University of Berlin (~1995–1999), and Munich (1999–2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Kim earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (-2011), studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld (born 1944) specializes in Sinology and art history. He studied at Stanford (BA ~1962–1966; PhD ~1972–1974) and Oregon. He held major posts at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and Princeton University (~2001–2018).

Jerzy Bańczerowski (1938–2026) was a linguist and Sinologist. He studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961), where he later served as department head (1969) and professor (1977–1991). He became a member of the Polish Academy of Sciences (~1994).

Jerzy Kuryłowicz (1895–1978) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Lviv (~1913–1923) and under Antoine Meillet (~1923–1925). He held posts at the University of Lviv (~1926–1946) and Jagiellonian University (~1946–1965).
